title: Growing in grace
note: Doctrine film, written 2026-11-27 for the Study Bible doctrine page on sanctification. Every fact comes from client/public/bible/doctrines/sanctification.json (definition, ot, nt, history, differ, errors, life); see facts.md. Scripture is the Berean Standard Bible, copied from client/public/bible/text/. Not yet recorded or read by James.

lines: You've trusted Christ, and you know you're forgiven. So why are you still fighting the same old sins?
And if God already accepts you, does it matter how you live?
The Bible answers both with one word. Sanctification.
To be holy is first to belong to God, set apart for him, and then to become like him.
Sanctification is the Holy Spirit's lifelong work of setting believers apart and making them like Jesus Christ.
It isn't justification, God's verdict that you're in the right, but the two never come apart.
Scripture speaks in two tenses. Believers already are sanctified, and they're being sanctified.
Paul wrote to a church full of factions and lawsuits, and still told them they'd been sanctified.
A saint, in the Bible, isn't a rare hero. It's any member of God's people.
One tense is still to come. When Christ appears, his people will be like him.
Holiness starts as God's claim. At Sinai he claims a whole people, holy because he chose them.
Leviticus calls Israel to be holy as God is holy, then to leave the edges of the harvest for the poor.
Holiness meant being like a God who cares for the poor.
Through Ezekiel, God promised his people a new heart, and his Spirit within them.
The night before he died, Jesus prayed for his disciples to be sanctified, and set himself apart for their sake.
Hebrews says believers were sanctified once for all by his sacrifice, and are still being sanctified.
Is grace a license to sin? No, says Paul, because believers have died with Christ and been set free from sin.
So who does the work, God or you? Paul says both.
Continue to work out your salvation, he writes. Then he says why.
For it is God who works in you to will and to act on behalf of His good purpose.
And the Spirit grows one fruit, not many. Love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control.

scripture.text: For it is God who works in you to will and to act on behalf of His good purpose.

lines: In the late fourth century, Gregory of Nyssa called perfection endless growth into God, because God has no end.
Augustine taught that holiness itself is a gift of grace, and that no one in this life is without sin.
Christians differ on how far holiness reaches in this life.
Reformed churches teach a decisive break with sin's rule, then slow growth, never finished in this life.
Lutherans stress living from forgiveness, a daily return to baptism, and not trusting your own progress.
Wesleyan and Holiness churches teach entire sanctification, a heart so full of love that the will is wholly God's, though not sinless perfection.
Keswick teaching calls for a decisive act of surrender and faith, then a life of consistent victory.
Catholics speak of grace growing through the sacraments, the Orthodox of theosis, lifelong growth into likeness to God.
So because you're already set apart and loved, failure doesn't undo your standing.
And because God means to make you like Christ, you can't make peace with your sin either.
The means are ordinary: Scripture, prayer, confession, the Lord's Supper, other believers, small duties, even hardship.
Growth is often slow, and others tend to see it before you do.
Zechariah saw a day when every cooking pot in Jerusalem would be holy.
Holiness reaches into how you pay a worker, treat the disabled, talk about people and forgive.
It all rests on a promise. The God who began the work will finish it.
The One who calls you is faithful, and He will do it.
Christians press on, not to earn the day Christ appears, but because it's coming.

scripture.text: The One who calls you is faithful, and He will do it.
